title: Polyglot SDK resilience playbook: pagination offsets, retries, and streaming backpressure
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Context: As Redwood rolls out richer streaming surfaces (structured streaming, tool-calls, incremental embeddings) we need a concise, actionable product playbook that sets required behaviors for Python, TypeScript, and Go clients. This ticket synthesizes requirements (pagination semantics, retry budgets, streaming resume, and backpressure) driven by production incidents, partner integrations, and SDK stability goals.

Goals: Provide clear, implementable requirements for SDK teams so: (1) developers can rely on consistent pagination semantics across languages, (2) retries are predictable and safe across idempotent and non-idempotent endpoints, and (3) streaming APIs expose a simple resume/backpressure story that minimizes application-level complexity.

Non-goals: This ticket does not mandate specific transport libraries for each language, nor does it prescribe kernel/runtime-level batching behavior on the server. Those are engineering implementation decisions.

Stakeholders: PM (Asha), SDK leads (Marco, Elena Rivera, Priya Singh), Runtime/ENG (Kunal Mehta), Security (Samir Rao), Developer Experience (Luca Moretti).

Constraints: Backwards compatibility with existing stable endpoints; low-latency SR for hosted customers; retention of minimal API surface so third-party clients can implement easily.

Deliverables: (1) Playbook doc with normative sections for pagination, retry, streaming resume, and compatibility matrix; (2) Acceptance criteria and test harness specs; (3) Example snippets for Python/TS/Go; (4) Migration notes for customers and SDK changelog templates.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Pagination: All three official SDKs expose a unified iterator-based pagination abstraction that supports both page-token and offset semantics. Iterator must allow 'seek' to a server-provided opaque cursor and be able to surface end-of-stream vs transient error distinctly.

2) Retry policy: SDK default behavior matches server-provided Retry-Control header guidelines: automatic retries only for idempotent GET-like endpoints and for POST endpoints only when server returns explicit retry-after or indicates safe-to-retry. Backoff is jittered exponential with caps documented in the playbook.

3) Streaming resume: Streaming APIs (chat/streaming-generate/embeddings-stream) expose a resume token in the stream footer. SDKs must attempt a single transparent resume by reconnecting with the resume token; if resume fails, SDK surfaces a resumable error code and a clear migration path.

4) Backpressure handling: Client libraries must provide a simple mechanism to apply backpressure on streaming consumers (push-based SDKs expose pause/resume hooks; pull-based SDKs expose async iterators that block on consumer demand). Examples included for Python async iterators, TS async generator, and Go channels.

5) Compatibility: The playbook includes a compatibility matrix that lists minimum supported client versions for each server contract and a deprecation policy (90-day notice for breaking contract changes).

6) Tests: Each SDK repo has automated tests that validate pagination resume, retry-window behavior under synthetic transient failures, and stream resume scenarios in CI. Test harness recipes provided in the doc.
7) Documentation: Code snippets and migration guidance for customers included in a single PR to the public docs repo and SDK CHANGELOG templates completed.
scope_changes: Initial scope included custom cursor encodings per-language. Decided to standardize on server-opaque base64 cursors to avoid drift and simplify cross-lang support.
Dropped: forcing clients to implement a persistent local queue for offline resume — marked as future enhancement (post-release).
decisions: Use server-opaque cursors (base64) for resume and pagination, no client-side decoding required.
Idempotency tokens: SDKs will expose helpers to generate and attach idempotency tokens for mutating calls; servers will accept and dedupe when marked idempotent.
Retries: default SDK policy will retry only safe operations; provide explicit opt-in for aggressive retries with a documented risk section.
Streaming resume: best-effort single-resume approach to balance complexity and ROI; multi-chunk resume left out of scope for v1.
Backpressure: adopt dual-model: push-mode exposes pause()/resume(), pull-mode exposes async iterator semantics across languages.
updates: 2026-03-04: Draft outline circulated to SDK leads; initial feedback: Go team requests clearer channel semantics for blocking reads.

2026-03-12: Design reviewed API examples; accepted TS and Python snippets; requested Go example refactor to use context cancellation semantics.
